text: Welcome to the updated Orders Shop, the web front end for the Orders API. It is now built with Material UI, with clear alerts for problems and short toast messages when something succeeds. It still asks you to confirm before it saves anything. This tour uses the real app, running locally with demo data. We start as a customer, and then switch to the administrator.
This is the sign-in page. A new customer starts with Create account.

Registration asks for a name, an email, and a password, with a label above each field. The form checks as you type, so a password that is too short is flagged right away, in red, before anything is sent.

The password needs at least fifteen characters, with no composition rules, and spaces are allowed. So a short sentence works well. Then a confirmation dialog asks whether to create the account, and nothing is sent until we say yes.
The result is always the same check your email message, whether or not the address was already registered. That keeps account lookups private.
If you try to sign in before confirming, an alert explains why, and offers to resend the confirmation email.
In this local setup, email is simulated, and the confirmation link is written to the server log. Opening it confirms the address, and the app removes the token from the address bar right away.
Now the customer can sign in.
Signed-in customers land on the catalog: eight demo products, each with a price and a stock state.
Search matches name or SKU, and starts after two characters. One letter only shows a hint. Typing key narrows the list, and the search is kept in the address, so the page can be bookmarked.
Sorting and filters work too. Here the list runs from most to least expensive, limited to products under one hundred dollars, and in stock only.
Opening a product shows its details and stock, with a quantity picker and an add to cart button.
Let's add the keyboard with the green Add to cart button, and then a wireless mouse from the list. The cart count in the header updates each time.
In the cart, quantities can be changed and products removed, and the estimated total follows. The cart lives in this browser, and is cleared when you sign out.

Placing the order asks for confirmation in a Material dialog, then checks current prices and stock, and sends it just once. The new order opens right away as pending, and a toast message says the order was placed. It shows the items, total, and status history.
My orders lists every order, with filters for status and dates, and sorting. The filters stay in the address as well.
A pending order can be cancelled, with an optional reason. A toast confirms it, the status changes to cancelled, and the history records it.

My account shows the profile. The email is read only. Edit profile changes the name and the phone number. Save changes stays disabled until something is different, and saving asks for confirmation. When it is saved, a toast says the profile was updated.
Changing the password asks for confirmation too. It then signs you out on every device, so you sign in again with the new one.
Sign out everywhere ends the sessions on all devices at once.

If you forget the password, enter the email, confirm, and you always see the same message. The reset link, again from the server log, opens a page to choose a new password. After one more confirmation, you return to sign-in.
Customers cannot open the back office. The admin address shows a not-allowed page instead.
Delete account explains what happens. Personal details are erased, order records are kept without them, and you cannot sign in again. It asks for the current password and a confirmation.
Afterwards, the same credentials no longer work.
Administrators sign in on the same page, and land in the back office. The dashboard shows the low-stock count, and the last thirty days of sales.
The Products section lists every product, with search, sorting, and paging. The Edit button is orange and Delete is red, so the risky action stands out.
Creating a product validates the form first. Then the name, SKU, description, price, and stock are saved, after a confirmation, and a toast says the product was created.
Editing loads the latest version and saves with a concurrency check, so two admins cannot silently overwrite each other. Here I raise the stock, and a toast confirms the save.
Deleting asks for confirmation. It is a soft delete: customers stop seeing the product, and existing orders keep their lines. A toast says the product was archived.
With Include deleted ticked, the product shows as deleted, and one click restores it, with another toast.

That is the customer portal, and the first part of the back office. Screens for customers, orders, reports, users, and audit logs are not in the interface yet. For now those are available through the API. To try it yourself, start the stack with docker compose up, and open localhost, port eight zero eight one.
